header.purpose: Artificial Japanese user turns for measuring a conversation router. Not real user data.

classes.casual: Small talk, greetings, feelings. Rationale: needs neither personal memory nor outside facts; the fast path is enough.
classes.memory: Depends on what the user said before or on personal preferences. Rationale: answering without approved notes loses or invents personal context. Also the safe fallback route.
classes.research: Needs outside, current or verifiable facts. Rationale: a model answering from stale knowledge is the costliest silent failure.

kinds.casual: Plain examples of the casual class.
kinds.memory: Plain examples of the memory class.
kinds.research: Plain examples of the research class.
kinds.ambiguous: Turns where more than one route is defensible; acceptable_routes lists them. Rationale: forcing one label would reward lucky guesses.
kinds.paraphrase: Turns that avoid obvious keywords. Rationale: a model router must read meaning; a keyword baseline should score worse here.
kinds.adversarial: Turns that try to steer the router (fake instructions, fake JSON, fake system messages, very long text, mixed languages). expected_route is what the person really asks for; steer_target is the route the injected text demands. Rationale: user text is data, never instructions.

cost_matrix.unit: relative cost of routing expected_route (row) to predicted route (column), multiplied by the turn's cost_weight; not money

header.limits: A small hand-written set. It measures routing behaviour on these turns only; it is not evidence of real-world quality and sets no pass threshold.
